subject: Coord: triple-stakeholder rolling demo windows (US / EU / APAC)

Subject: Exec demo request — coordinating across US/EU/APAC (late Oct)

Hi Priya,

Thanks for the intro earlier. We're ready to schedule a 60–90 minute executive demo of Redwood for OpenPayments. Our stakeholders: myself (US, SF), Hiroshi Saito (Tokyo) and the EU payments lead (Lisbon, CEST). We want the product overview + short deep-dive and time for Q&A with our CTO and Head of Ops.

Target window: late Oct (around Oct 26–29). Two constraints to flag up front:
- We want at least one slot where our US execs can attend live with EU participants (we can stretch into the evening PT)
- We prefer to avoid any calendar confusion around daylight savings — EU switches last Sunday in Oct; US switches in early Nov. If possible please propose times that are robust against those transitions.

Can you share a few rolling-window options that work for your execs and also any fallback plan if one exec drops from the session? We may need to do a short second session for APAC-only deep-dive.

Thanks — feel free to propose an approach (single long session vs split sessions).

Best,
Olivia
Olivia Chan
Director, Platform Partnerships — OpenPayments
olivia.chan@openpayments.com
From: priya_natarajan@redwood.example.com

Subject: Re: Exec demo request — coordinating across US/EU/APAC (late Oct)

Hi Olivia — thanks for the context. Quick reply with two approaches and availability:

1) Single anchored session (90m) — one calendar invite, all execs join.
   - Pros: one run, one recording, consistent Q&A.
   - Cons: tradeoffs on local business hours for at least one region (likely APAC late).

2) Rolling/demo rotation (3 x ~40m overlapping blocks) — US+EU block -> EU+APAC block -> APAC deep-dive.
   - Pros: minimizes local-hour pain, allows APAC-focused follow-up, easier to limit exec time.
   - Cons: requires coordination for handoff and short, focused overlap.

Because you called out DST risk, I recommend option 2 (rolling rotation) — gives us a clean fallback if an exec needs to drop or if someone's calendar shifts unexpectedly. Below are tentative windows (all times in UTC with local conversions). I've kept them outside the immediate DST cutover week to avoid ambiguity, but flagged the dates.

Proposed dates (pick one): Oct 27 (preferred), Oct 28.

Option A — Rolling rotation (Oct 27)
- Block 1 — US + EU (40m): 2026-10-27 17:00–17:40 UTC (10:00 PT / 13:00 ET / 18:00 CEST)
- Hand-off (10m overlap)
- Block 2 — EU + APAC (40m): 2026-10-27 17:30–18:10 UTC (19:30 CEST / 02:30 JST)
- APAC deep-dive follow-up (optional 30m) — 2026-10-28 01:30–02:00 UTC (09:30 JST)

Option B — Single full session (90m): 2026-10-27 17:00–18:30 UTC (10:00 PT / 19:00 CEST / 02:30 JST next day)

Notes:
- I invited Karthik (serving runtime lead) and Laura (GS lead) on CC to confirm availability.
- If you confirm exec names and preferred date, we will block these slots and then send calendar invites with clear local time conversion.

Action we need from you: confirm preferred date (Oct 27 or Oct 28), preferred approach (rolling vs single), and a list of execs who must be on the main session.

Thanks,
Priya Natarajan
Partnerships — Redwood Inference
priya_natarajan@redwood.example.com

Quick note from infra/ops perspective: option 2 (rolling) is preferable. A few operational details to confirm — I pasted as bullets so we can lock them in:
- Staffing: we'll have one product lead in each block (me — infra; Laura — integrations; Marcus — sales engineering)
- Recording: we will record Block 1 and Block 2 separately and stitch recordings for your team.
- Fallback: if an exec in the US can't attend Block 1, we can replay highlights for them in the APAC follow-up.
- Calendar invites: prefer to send separate invites for each block with explicit local times and an "overlap reminder" in the invite text so participants know when hand-off occurs.

Also — please keep the APAC deep-dive optional; if Hiroshi prefers a daytime JST slot, we can propose Oct 28 morning JST, otherwise we can do the short follow-up immediately after Block 2.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer | Head of Serving Runtime — Redwood Inference
